Playbook.name: FortiGate — Internal Host Beaconing to Malicious/C2 Domain (DNS) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: An internal host repeatedly queried domains the FortiGate DNS filter REDIRECTED (blocked as malicious/C2) - 10+ queries to a flagged domain in the window. Triage question: is an internal host infected and beaconing to C2, or is this benign software hitting a domain that is over-categorised?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: DNS beaconing to C2 indicates an active infection; even though redirected, the host is compromised and trying to reach its controller.

Assets.AssetType: FortiGate perimeter and internal firewalls (HQ + DR)
Internal server and user segments behind the FortiGate

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: FortiGate logs shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-fortinet_fortigate.* (verified live).

Fields: fortinet.firewall.subtype (ips/dns/...), fortinet.firewall.action, fortinet.firewall.severity, fortinet.firewall.attack, fortinet.firewall.srccountry/dstcountry ('Reserved' = RFC1918 internal), fortinet.firewall.cfgpath, dns.question.name, source.ip, destination.ip, destination.port.

Signal.Name: C2 DNS beaconing
Signal.Details: subtype dns, action redirect, >=10 queries to a flagged domain; known infra excluded.

Input.name: $domain
Input.description: The flagged domain (dns.question.name) if in the alert.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Redirected DNS = the filter caught it, but the QUERY means something on the host wants that domain; distinguish malware beaconing from benign apps hitting a mis-categorised domain (e.g. a legit CDN flagged).

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the internal host is infected and beaconing to C2, or querying a benign-but-miscategorised domain.

Step.name: Beacon cadence and domain set for this host
Step.Purpose: Regular, repeated queries to one flagged domain = beaconing; a one-off or human-driven pattern differs.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.log-* | WHERE fortinet.firewall.subtype == "dns" AND fortinet.firewall.action == "redirect" AND source.ip == "$source_ip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS queries = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY dns.question.name | SORT queries DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: Steady queries evenly spread across the window to a random-looking or known-bad domain = beaconing. A burst then silence, or a well-known domain, suggests benign software or a miscategorisation. DGA-style names strongly indicate malware.

Step.name: Is the host also making external connections (exfil/C2 over IP)
Step.Purpose: A beaconing host may also reach C2 directly by IP; check its accepted outbound connections.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.traffic-* | WHERE source.ip == "$source_ip" AND fortinet.firewall.action == "accept" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS conns = COUNT(*), ext_dsts = COUNT_DISTINCT(destination.ip), dcountries = VALUES(fortinet.firewall.dstcountry), dports = VALUES(destination.port) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Accepted outbound to foreign/high-risk countries or unusual ports alongside the DNS beaconing strengthens the C2 conclusion. Normal browsing patterns weaken it.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows regular beacon cadence to a bad/DGA domain, or INV-02 shows corroborating external C2-like connections.
Node.Result: True Positive (Infected Host Beaconing - isolate and IR)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows the flagged domain is a well-known benign service (CDN/analytics) queried by normal software.
INV-01 shows queries to a flagged ad/tracking domain by a browser (benign but policy-blocked).
Beaconing-like cadence to an unclear domain with no corroboration.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-FGDNS-BEACON, INV-02-FGDNS-CONNS to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Benign software or browsing hitting a domain the filter over-categorises (CDN, analytics, ads).

Indicators.Item: Flagged domain is a known-benign service.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the domain reputation; propose recategorisation/allowlist.

TruePositive.Definition: An infected internal host beaconing to command-and-control.

Indicators.Item: Regular beacon cadence to a bad/DGA domain.
Corroborating external connections to high-risk destinations.
Host has no legitimate reason to query the domain.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate the host; capture memory/process for the beaconing malware.
Block the domain/IP estate-wide; open IR; hunt for the same beacon on other hosts.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A misconfigured internal tool repeatedly querying a blocked domain (e.g. stale integration endpoint).

Indicators.Item: A known app repeatedly resolving a decommissioned/blocked endpoint.

SOCAction.Item: Fix the tool's endpoint config; document.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host if beaconing confirmed; capture volatile evidence.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Malware analysis on the host; hunt the beacon across the estate; eradicate.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Keep DNS filtering enforcing; add the C2 to blocklists; EDR sweep for the malware family.

QualityChecks.Check: action 'redirect' = the DNS filter blocked/sinkholed. Rule excludes known internal DNS infra.
Suppression 24h per source - repeated daily alerts = infection not remediated.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host isolated and cleaned; C2 blocked; estate swept; no other infections.
